summary: Goldman Sachs open-sourced the Python client for their internal derivatives pricing and risk engine, so you get a package that wraps Monte Carlo, tree, and PDE solvers for exotic options behind a clean, typed API — the math is the real artifact, twenty-five years of quant modeling distilled into callable functions. The catch is that every backend call requires a GS institutional client ID and secret, so it's closer to a reference implementation you can read than a tool you can actually run on your laptop, which is the opposite of the local-first, composable stack I try to build. Still, skimming the API surface is a useful reminder of how much structure you inherit when a shop has been solving the same pricing and hedging problems for decades, and the stochastic primitives overlap enough with the simulation work I do in bioinformatics that the abstractions translate.
